flashcards.front: Rule 1: LAWS
flashcards.back: Every employee is expected to be familiar with and obey all public laws, company or departmental rules, instructions, specifications etc. covering or relating to their conduct as an agent of the company, or the work on which they are engaged. Lack of such knowledge will not serve to excuse any failure to observe them.

flashcards.front: Rule 2: LOYALTY
flashcards.back: A steadfast loyalty to the companies interest is demanded from every employee, in order that the company may faithfully perform the duties with which it is charged.

flashcards.front: Rule 3: HONESTY
flashcards.back: The company expects and requires absolute honesty from every employee in all dealings with the public, the company, and fellow employees.

flashcards.front: Rule 4: EFFORT
flashcards.back: The company expects from each employee a maximum of efficient effort on every undertaking assigned to them.

flashcards.front: Rule 5: SERVICE
flashcards.back: Every employee must guard against unnecessary interruption or interference with the service.

flashcards.front: Rule 6: ORDER
flashcards.back: No employee may order, purchase, rent or in any manner acquire in the name of the company, or commit it to acquire, property, goods or services of any nature except as regularly or specifically authorized.

flashcards.front: Rule 7: PROPERTY
flashcards.back: No employee may loan, give, sell or destroy or otherwise dispose of the company's property, equipment, supplies or services except as regularly or specifically authorized and must disburse, use and account for such property etc. in exact accordance with his or her instructions.

flashcards.front: Rule 8: RESPECT
flashcards.back: Employees as such must at all times respect the personal property, rights and privileges of other persons, and avoid any act, statement or neglect which may give offense or involve the company in controversies or litigation of any kind.

flashcards.front: Rule 9: FUNDS
flashcards.back: Employees to whom are entrusted funds of the company will be held personally responsible to safeguard and disburse them in exact accordance with the instructions on this subject.

flashcards.front: Rule 10: PREVENT INJURY
flashcards.back: To prevent injury to persons or property the company requires each employee to exercise every practicable precaution in performing his work, to report any condition or any practice, negligence or incompetence of others which endangers himself, the public or other workmen and to aid and assist any employee or non-employee who may become injured during the course of our work.

flashcards.front: Rule 11: DRUGS
flashcards.back: The use of intoxicating beverages or drugs, engaging in games of chance, placing bets, bookmaking or other unlawful acts are not permitted on the company's premises at any time or elsewhere while on company business.

flashcards.front: Rule 12: BUILDING
flashcards.back: Additions to, removals from or changes in any respect of the specified or original design of building, equipment or other plant, is not permitted except as duly authorized and instructed.

flashcards.front: Rule 13: ENGAGE BUSINESS
flashcards.back: Employees shall not engage in business or act as employee or agent of any person or concern to the detriment directly or indirectly of the company's interest.

flashcards.front: Rule 14: PR
flashcards.back: Making unauthorized statements in the public or press regarding company affairs is not permitted.

flashcards.front: Rule 15: RECOMMENDATION EQUIPMENT
flashcards.back: As an agent of the company, employees shall not give recommendation or testimonial for any equipment, material or process except to the company.

flashcards.front: Rule 16: EXHIBIT RECORDS
flashcards.back: No employee shall exhibit company records, plans or correspondence, or convey the information contained therein to any person unless specifically authorized to do so.

flashcards.front: Rule 17: TESTIMONY
flashcards.back: Employee's shall not volunteer expert testimony without proper approval.

flashcards.front: Rule 18: TIMESHEETS
flashcards.back: No employee shall make, certify or approve any record, statement or report known by him to be false.

flashcards.front: Rule 19: COMPANY MATERIALS
flashcards.back: No employee shall use the company's materials, vehicles, equipment or other property for personal purposes without permission.

flashcards.front: Rule 20: PROPERTY SUBSCRIBER
flashcards.back: No employee shall use the property of a subscriber or other person or concern for company or personal purposes without permission.

flashcards.front: Rule 21: ABSENT
flashcards.back: Employees must notify their respective supervisors at any time when it is necessary for them to be absent or tardy.

flashcards.front: Rule 22: SOLICIT
flashcards.back: No employee shall solicit subscriptions among employees during working hours without permission.

flashcards.front: Rule 23: EXPLOSIVES
flashcards.back: Unnecessarily bringing or permitting explosives or combustibles in or near to the company's buildings or premises is not permitted.

flashcards.front: Rule 24: SMOKING
flashcards.back: Smoking is not allowed in any company owned or leased property at any time.

flashcards.front: Rule 25: COMPANY NAME
flashcards.back: No employee shall use the company's name or account to purchase goods for personal use.

flashcards.front: Rule 26: PERMISSION TO PURCHASE
flashcards.back: Employees shall not, without permission, purchase directly, any supplies or equipment which should be obtained on requisition.

flashcards.front: Rule 27: NON-STANDARD EQUIPMENT
flashcards.back: No employee shall except from agents or others, non-standard equipment, tools or materials for trial or demonstration.

flashcards.front: Rule 28: LOAN BADGES
flashcards.back: Employees are not permitted to loan badges, books, tools or property of the company.

flashcards.front: Rule 29: ASSIGN WAGES
flashcards.back: Employees may not assign their wages or otherwise involve the company in their personal affairs.

flashcards.front: Rule 30: DAMAGE
flashcards.back: Employees shall report promptly and in accordance with instructions, any accidental damage they may have caused or which has come to their attention.

flashcards.front: Rule 31: TRIM
flashcards.back: Permission to work on private property or to trim or cut trees on the highway or elsewhere should be obtained before such work is started.

flashcards.front: What does a Class 2 Type 1 Rubber Glove tag look like?
flashcards.back: Yellow Tag, embossed with an 'F'.

flashcards.front: What voltages do Class 2 Type 1 (Type F) protect against?
flashcards.back: 34,500 Volts AC phase to phase / 20,000 Volts AC phase to ground.

flashcards.front: What are the 5 tests for Rubber Gloves?
flashcards.back: 1. Date, 2. Stretch, 3. Finger roll, 4. Resiliency, 5. Air tightness.

flashcards.front: 188A Voltage Detector Ranges?
What does the GREEN LED mean on the 188A self test?
flashcards.back: It means the basic circuitry is working properly.

flashcards.front: What does the RED LED mean on the 188A during a test?
flashcards.back: Hazardous voltage is detected. DO NOT PROCEED.

flashcards.front: What ANSI standard applies to Safety Glasses?
flashcards.back: ANSI Z87.

flashcards.front: What ANSI standard applies to Boots?
flashcards.back: ANSI Z41 (Impacts up to 75 lbs, crushing force of 2500 lbs).

flashcards.front: What are the specs for a Hard Hat?
flashcards.back: Type I Class E, ANSI 89.1. Protects against 20,000 v (incidental contact). Replace every 5 years.

flashcards.front: What are the gases listed under the acronym `Pagan hammer bc`?
flashcards.back: Propane, Acetelyne, Gasoline, Alcohol, Natural gas, Hydrogen, Ammonia, Mapp gas, Methane, Ethelene, Refrigerants, Butane, Carbon Monoxide.

flashcards.front: What are the 8 Steps of Quality? (Hint: BCCDOSST)
flashcards.back: 1. Bond, 2. Conductors, 3. Close, 4. Drip collar, 5. Openings, 6. Support conductors, 7. Support cable, 8. Tape ends/nozzle.

flashcards.front: List some elements of Vault Safety.
flashcards.back: Tip Splice, No Spark Phone, RDA III A, Glow in dark arrows, Reverse thread light bulb, Key from CO tech, 2 Fire Extinguishers (water and Halon for electric).

flashcards.front: What is OHM's Law?
flashcards.back: The relationship between voltage, current and resistance in a circuit. It takes 1 volt to push 1 amp through 1 ohm of resistance.

flashcards.front: What is Capacitance?
flashcards.back: The ability of a conductor to hold a charge. It has high resistance to DC, and low resistance to AC.

flashcards.front: What are the 5 types of Grounding?
flashcards.back: 1. Power Co. MGN, 2. Conductor from MGN, 3. Metallic threaded pipe, 4. Electric meter, 5. Ground rod.

flashcards.front: Drop Clearance minimums for Railroad and Pool?
flashcards.back: Railroad is 27. Pool is 22.

flashcards.front: What does a Black coil indicate?
flashcards.back: Standard protection

flashcards.front: What is D Encapsulant used for?
flashcards.back: Buried and fiber.

flashcards.front: What is pipe tight used for?
flashcards.back: Pipe tight is used for sealing, but NOT on regulators.

flashcards.front: What does an RF power of -20dBmV or greater indicate?
flashcards.back: No RF signal.

flashcards.front: What does an Inductor do?
flashcards.back: Preserves current by storing energy in a magnetic field (ex. Load Coil). Load coils increase inductance.

flashcards.front: What is the Drop Wire horizontal and vertical clearance from power at a house attachment?
flashcards.back: Horizontal: 40 inches. Vertical: 18 inches.

flashcards.front: What is the Litespan 2000?
flashcards.back: A Multiplexer. It is a SONET-based system.

flashcards.front: What is the purpose of Loading?
flashcards.back: To increase loop resistance and bring the pair back into phase.

flashcards.front: What frequencies do Load Coils block?
flashcards.back: Frequencies between 3,400 Hz and 4,200 Hz.

flashcards.front: If you see a rainbow on the water near or in a manhole, what should you assume?
flashcards.back: Assume gasoline. There is no need to test if you smell it.

flashcards.front: How do you test a Dry manhole hole with an explosimeter?
flashcards.back: Put the sampling hose at head level, use 8 squeezes minimum.

flashcards.front: What are the minimum Air Pressure PSI guidelines for cables?
flashcards.back:
Aerial: 2 psi
Buried: 3 psi
Underground: 5 psi
Submarine: 6 psi
End pipe: 7 psi

flashcards.front: What are the 7 Deadly Sins (Plus the unofficial 8th)?
flashcards.back:
1. Working aloft without hard hat.
2. Working aloft without 188A testing.
3. Bucket without lanyard/chocks.
4. Ladder without safety straps.
5. Manhole without blower or RDA III.
6. Working without safety glasses.
7. No seatbelt.
*8. Using cell phone while driving.

flashcards.front: List forms of Mechanical Protection.
flashcards.back: Sealed closures, Encapsulated splices, Jell filled cable, Air pressure, Plant separation (Conduit, inner duct, inner dam, U guard, tree guard).

flashcards.front: List forms of Electrical Protection.
flashcards.back: Bonding, Grounding, Ground rods, IJ's, Choke splices, Coils, Carbons, Fuses, Fusible links, Minimum approach distances.

flashcards.front: What is the accuracy and response time of the RDA IIIA?
flashcards.back: Accuracy within 5% of calibrated level. Response time of 10 seconds at 10% of Lowest Explosive Level.

flashcards.front: What gas is used for Daily Calibration of the RDA 3A?
flashcards.back: 5000 PPM (.5%) Methane gas from a GREEN cylinder. NEVER USE C GAS.

flashcards.front: What happens if the Remote Sensing Unit (RSU) gets soaked or submerged?
flashcards.back: It will damage or render the gas sensor inoperable.

flashcards.front: What is the order of the Rubber Gloves 'Spiel' expected at the exam?
flashcards.back: 1. Bag, 2. Cotton Liners, 3. Leather Gloves, 4. Rubber Gloves.

flashcards.front: What does the Rib at the gauntlet of a rubber glove do?
flashcards.back: It is the Flash Over Dam preventing rain or moisture from creating a pathway for possible electrocution.

flashcards.front: What are the 5 tests for a Hard Hat?
flashcards.back:
1. Resiliency (Bend Brim)
2. Visual (cracks, cuts)
3. Harness (1.5 inch clearance)
4. Fit (Should not fall off)
5. Date (5 years once put into service)

flashcards.front: What is Repeater type 809?
flashcards.back: Gas tube protected, 12T1S - 239.

flashcards.front: In an SLC 96 system, what does the TAU (Time Assignment Unit) do in Mode 2?
flashcards.back: Assigns Priority to calls and keeps a log of blocked calls. Mode 2 uses 48 dial tones for 96 customers.

flashcards.front: What does Mode 3 of SLC 96 utilize?
flashcards.back: It utilizes an MXU (Multiplexer Unit). It has 48 circuits and can have a DT PayPhone Line.

flashcards.front: Why is Friction Tape not used in underground wraps?
flashcards.back: Because it is gasoline soluble. It is used as a final aerial wrap.

flashcards.front: What is Sterine Core solder used for?
flashcards.back: It is used for wiping lead to lead, and is also used to check serrations on long nose pliers.

flashcards.front: On a 300 TYPE block, how does the 50 pair block count work?
flashcards.back: Counts Top to Bottom. Odd on the left, Even on the right. Cross wired on the right, test contacts on the left.

flashcards.front: What does a Sidekick test set's Leakage Test do?
flashcards.back: It uses 135 VDC to punch through the oxide layer of a fault on a dry pair.

flashcards.front: What does the Shortstop test set use?
flashcards.back: It uses TDR (Time Domain Reflectometry) with a range of 2000-2500 feet.

flashcards.front: How much water will 1 PSI keep out?
flashcards.back: 1 PSI will keep out 2 feet of water.

flashcards.front: What system monitors the remote Manhole pressure transducers?
flashcards.back: The Sparta System monitors the transducers placed out in the manholes.

flashcards.front: What is the rule for placing signs regarding speed limits 35MPH and over?
flashcards.back: Place sign 10 times the speed limit back. For example, 35 MPH = sign should be 350 feet back.

flashcards.front: Can you use your truck as a shield?
flashcards.back: No, do not use your truck as a shield. Park beyond the manhole, in the same direction as traffic.

flashcards.front: What is Electrolysis in cables and how is it fought?
flashcards.back: Electrolysis is stray DC current traveling along the lead sheath, decaying it. It is fought using Bonding/Grounding, Magnesium Strips, IJ's, and Anodes.

flashcards.front: What is unique about the 134A1A Protected Interior Terminal?
flashcards.back: It is carbon protected, and there is NO loss of dial tone (dt) when the fuse is pulled, unlike the 190.

flashcards.front: What is a Trac Closure?
flashcards.back: A toolless reenterable aerial closure.

flashcards.front: What is the function of the LSU (Line Switch Unit)?
flashcards.back: It directs automatic switching to a shared protection line during a failure.

flashcards.front: What does the SSU (Special Service Unit) do?
flashcards.back: Provides delayed processing signal for PBX trunks, synchronizes timing on circuits, and quiets channel noise.

flashcards.front: What occurs if the PU (Power Unit) shuts down?
flashcards.back: It must be removed for 5 seconds and reseated.

flashcards.front: What is the TRU (Transmit / Receive Unit) responsible for?
flashcards.back: It encodes channel sampling to PCM on transmit, and decodes/demultiplexes the PCM signal on receive.

flashcards.front: What does a complete Litespan 2000 system at the Central Office control?
flashcards.back: It controls 5 remote terminals (3 east, 2 west) for a total of 10,080 pots lines.

flashcards.front: What is the maximum Ground Wire length for an ONT and a NI (Network Interface)?
flashcards.back: 150 feet maximum for a Fiber ONT. 20 feet maximum for a copper NI.

flashcards.front: What is the RJ45 jack?
flashcards.back: It is an 8-position, 8-contact jack, utilized with 9 resistors.

flashcards.front: What is the difference between Single-Mode and Multi-Mode fiber?
flashcards.back: Single-Mode has a smaller core for less light loss, used for high-speed data, and has YELLOW markings. Multi-Mode has ORANGE markings and is of lesser quality (should not be used anymore).

flashcards.front: What are the characteristics of a Fiber Ribbon Cable?
flashcards.back: It contains 6, 12, or 24 fibers. 12 fibers per tube, and 12 tubes per sheath.

flashcards.front: What are the specs of GPON vs BPON?
flashcards.back: GPON (Gigabit Passive Optical Network) transfers up to 300Gb using TDMA. BPON transfers up to 100Gb.

flashcards.front: Explain the downstream, upstream, and video nanometer (nm) waves in an optical network.
flashcards.back:
1490nm = downstream data (2.488 Gbits)
1310nm = upstream data (1.244 Gbits)
1550nm = video.

quizzes.question: During the testing of the voltage detector, the black conductive end cap can be left on the probe tip.
A false hazardous voltage reading can be caused by static discharge.
Anything that is in your work space and has the potential to be energized must be tested.
Performing a self test on the 188A must be done before testing for hazardous voltage.
